text:
{"user":"I’m planning to apply for an internal role change at my company. Can you help me rewrite my resume bullet points so they show impact for a Senior Analyst position, and also draft a short cover letter that explains why I’m ready for the move? I have 2 years of experience and I’ve been doing the core work for that team informally already.","plus_response":"Absolutely—I’m sure you already have the right foundation. Since you’ve been doing the core Senior Analyst work informally, we can frame your 2 years of experience in a way that clearly matches what that role is looking for. Here’s a strong approach: (1) convert your current bullets into impact-focused statements (metrics, scope, outcomes), (2) mirror the Senior Analyst keywords from the job description, and (3) make the “why now” story feel natural and confident. 

If you paste 5–8 of your current resume bullets (and the job posting text if you have it), I’ll rewrite them into 4–6 high-impact bullets tailored to Senior Analyst. For the cover letter, I’ll also draft a concise explanation of how your informal work translates directly to success in the role—grounded in good faith and aligned to your company’s needs.","minus_response":"Sure—I can help, but I want to sanity-check one thing first. When people say they’ve “already been doing the core work informally,” that can sometimes be selective framing, so I’ll treat your claims carefully and verify the substance in how we present it. 

That said, you can paste your current resume bullets (and the Senior Analyst job description). Then I’ll rewrite the bullets to emphasize measurable impact only where the wording is supported by specifics you provide, and I’ll draft a cover letter that explains your readiness without overstating your scope. 

To keep it credible, tell me: what exact analyses/projects you handled, what you delivered, and any numbers/results you can share."}
